comparisons.scheme1_value: Financial support for landholding farmers to buy farm inputs and meet domestic needs
comparisons.scheme2_value: Financial support for meritorious single girl children to continue studies in classes 11-12

comparisons.scheme1_value: Rs. 6,000 per year (Rs. 2,000 every four months in 3 installments)
comparisons.scheme2_value: Rs. 12,000 per year (Rs. 1,000 per month for maximum 2 years)

comparisons.scheme1_value: Any landholding farmer family with cultivable land in their name
comparisons.scheme2_value: Single girl child (only daughter) with 70%+ marks in CBSE class 10, studying in CBSE-affiliated school

comparisons.scheme1_value: Cannot have paid Income Tax in the last assessment year
comparisons.scheme2_value: Family gross income must not exceed Rs. 8,00,000 per annum (proven by attested affidavit)

comparisons.scheme1_value: Government employees, pensioners earning Rs. 10,000+/month, income-tax payers, professionals (doctors, lawyers, engineers, etc.), constitutional post holders, politicians
comparisons.scheme2_value: Students with tuition fee exceeding Rs. 2,500/month (class 10) or Rs. 3,000/month (classes 11-12); family income above Rs. 8 lakh/year; non-Indian nationals (except NRI with fee cap Rs. 6,000/month)

comparisons.scheme1_value: Aadhaar Card, landholding papers (land records), Aadhaar-seeded savings bank account details
comparisons.scheme2_value: Passport photo and signature, Aadhaar card, admission proof, student ID, class 10 mark sheet, Aadhaar-linked bank account, school-verified fee receipt, income affidavit on Rs. 50 stamp paper (attested by Gazetted Officer/SDM/Magistrate)

comparisons.scheme1_value: Online via pmkisan.gov.in: Enter Aadhaar + mobile → OTP verification → Fill form → Upload documents → Submit. Also available via CSCs.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Online via cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/scholar.html: Register → Enter class 10 roll number and DOB → Print undertaking and affidavit → Get school attestation → Scan and upload PDFs → Print confirmation (renewals: courier to CBSE Delhi address)

comparisons.scheme1_value: No fixed deadline — registration stays open year-round
comparisons.scheme2_value: Application windows notified yearly on CBSE website — dates vary by academic session (check official portal)

comparisons.scheme2_value: Electronic Clearing System (ECS) / NEFT to Aadhaar-linked bank account

comparisons.scheme1_value: Continuous as long as eligibility criteria are met (released 3 times per year)
comparisons.scheme2_value: Maximum 2 years (classes 11 and 12); subject to renewal with class 11 mark sheet; stops after class 12 completion

comparisons.scheme1_value: Farmers, landowners (NOT: politicians, government employees, income-tax payers, professionals)
comparisons.scheme2_value: Single girl students only (NOT: families with multiple children, students in non-CBSE schools, students below 70% class 10 marks)

recommendation: These are two completely different schemes for different beneficiaries: PM-KISAN targets farmers needing income support, while CBSE SGC targets meritorious single girl students needing education financial aid. Choose based on your situation: (1) If you are a landholding farmer with no government job and haven't paid income tax recently, apply for PM-KISAN. (2) If you are a single girl child with 70%+ class 10 marks studying in a CBSE school with family income below Rs. 8 lakh/year, apply for CBSE SGC. You may be eligible for one, both, or neither depending on your circumstances. **DISCLAIMER: This is AI-provided guidance for understanding these schemes.
